## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) on a cron schedule or once at a specific time. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction.
- vercel-cli: Deploy, manage, and develop projects on Vercel from the command line
- web-design-guidelines: Review UI code for Web Interface Guidelines compliance. Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices".
- next-best-practices: Next.js best practices - file conventions, RSC boundaries, data patterns, async APIs, metadata, error handling, route handlers, image/font optimization, bundling
- next-upgrade: Upgrade Next.js to the latest version following official migration guides and codemods
- vercel-react-best-practices: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering. This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code to ensure optimal performance patterns. Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.
- building-components: Guide for building modern, accessible, and composable UI components. Use when building new components, implementing accessibility, creating composable APIs, setting up design tokens, publishing to npm/registry, or writing component documentation.
- next-cache-components: Next.js 16 Cache Components - PPR, use cache directive, cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag
- vercel-composition-patterns: React composition patterns that scale. Use when refactoring components with boolean prop proliferation, building flexible component libraries, or designing reusable APIs. Triggers on tasks involving compound components, render props, context providers, or component architecture. Includes React 19 API changes.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, screen, or view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles via search_design_system, imports them, and assembles screens incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-design: Translates Figma designs into production-ready application code with 1:1 visual fidelity. Use when implementing UI code from Figma files, when user mentions "implement design", "generate code", "implement component", provides Figma URLs, or asks to build components matching Figma specs. For Figma canvas writes via `use_figma`, use `figma-use`.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-create-design-system-rules: Generates custom design system rules for the user's codebase. Use when user says "create design system rules", "generate rules for my project", "set up design rules", "customize design system guidelines", or wants to establish project-specific conventions for Figma-to-code workflows. Requires Figma MCP server connection.
- andrej-karpathy-skills:karpathy-guidelines: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Osijek, HR · Od 1990.
Hidrotehnika / Inženjering / Nadzor

Voda kao
infrastruktura,
projekt kao odgovornost.

Hidroing d.o.o. iz Osijeka izrađuje projektnu dokumentaciju, tehnička rješenja i stručni nadzor gradnje hidrotehničkih građevina — od vodoopskrbe i odvodnje do uređenja vodotoka i zaštite od štetnog djelovanja voda.

Projekti Usluge
H-001 / 16:10
[ Rekonstrukcija uređaja za pročišćavanje otpadnih voda — Osijek ]

Sustav upravljanja kvalitetom
01 — O tvrtki

Hidrotehnika je tiha disciplina — mjeri se stoljećima, a ne kvartalima.

Specijalizirani smo za izradu projektne dokumentacije i stručni nadzor svih vrsta hidrotehničkih građevina. Radimo od idejnih rješenja preko glavnih i izvedbenih projekata do nadzora izvođenja, uvijek u dijalogu s naručiteljem i prostorom.

Osnovano
1990. / Osijek
Licencirani inženjeri
6 ovlaštenih, 2 suradnika
Područje djelovanja
Hrvatska i regija
02 / Usluge

Od idejnog rješenja do predaje objekta.

Pokrivamo cijeli životni ciklus hidrotehničkog projekta. Ispod je skraćeni pregled — puna usluga i faze dostupne su na stranici usluga.

01
Vodoopskrba i odvodnja
Projektiranje mreža, crpnih stanica, spremnika i sustava odvodnje; rehabilitacija postojećih sustava.
→
02
Uređaji za pročišćavanje
Tehnološka i građevinska rješenja UPOV-a za naselja i industriju; od kompaktnih jedinica do velikih postrojenja.
→
03
Uređenje vodotoka
Regulacije rijeka i potoka, obaloutvrde, retencije — u službi sigurnosti i krajolika.
→
04
Riječne luke i pristaništa
Projektiranje i nadzor lučkih građevina u riječnom prometu, uključujući pristane i manipulativne površine.
→
05
Studije utjecaja na okoliš
Izrada SUO i dokumentacije za ocjenu potrebe procjene utjecaja zahvata na okoliš.
→
06
Stručni nadzor gradnje
Ovlašteni nadzor izvođenja svih navedenih građevina u skladu s propisima i dobrom praksom.
→
Sve usluge

Odabrani projekti.

Navodnjavanje · Studija + projekt
04 / Tim

Mali tim, dug stručni staž.

Osam inženjera i suradnika s ovlaštenjima Hrvatske komore inženjera građevinarstva. Svaki projekt vodi odgovorni inženjer od prvog sastanka do predaje.

S terena.

Fotografije s gradilišta, pregleda i primopredaja. Kronika svakodnevice tvrtke.

Početna / O nama

Tri i pol desetljeća u jednoj disciplini.

Hidroing je projektantska i inženjerska kuća iz Osijeka. Radimo isključivo s vodom — kao resursom, kao rizikom i kao dijelom krajolika. Ova stranica govori o tome kako smo stigli ovdje.

— Manifest
Voda ne prašta improvizaciju.
Zato projektiramo polako, a odlučujemo uporno.
01 / Povijest

Kronologija.

Od osnivanja u Osijeku 1990. do referentnih projekata u regiji. Nekoliko trenutaka koji oblikuju to što tvrtka danas jest.

1990
Osnivanje

Osnovan ured u Osijeku.

Tri inženjera i jedan stol. Prvi poslovi — manje regulacije potoka u okolici grada i kanalizacijski priključci.

1998
Obnova

Obnova vodoopskrbe u Slavoniji i Baranji.

Poslijeratna obnova donosi prve velike projekte vodoopskrbnih magistrala i rekonstrukcije crpnih stanica.

2006
UPOV

Prvi UPOV — Belišće.

Projekt uređaja za pročišćavanje s klasičnom aktivacijom, 12.000 ES. Početak specijalizacije u tehnološkim linijama.

2014
EU fondovi

Prvi projekti sufinancirani iz EU sredstava.

Ulazak Hrvatske u EU donosi nove standarde i financijske okvire. Tvrtka prolazi certifikaciju prema ISO 9001 i uspostavlja interni sustav praćenja kvalitete.

2019
Vodotoci

Program zaštite od poplave — Karašica.

Projektiranje 11 km obrambenog nasipa i crpne stanice 2,4 m³/s. Jedan od većih projekata zaštite od voda u istočnoj Hrvatskoj.

2023
Danas

UPOV Osijek — II. faza u pogonu.

Rekonstruirani gradski uređaj pokriva 180.000 ES uz tercijarni stupanj. Tvrtka zapošljava osam stalnih članova tima.

02 / Priznanja

Priznanja i odabrane pohvale.

Nagrade su sporedni proizvod dobrog rada — ali pomažu potvrditi smjer.

2024
Nagrada Hrvatske komore inženjera građevinarstva
Za projekt UPOV Osijek — II. faza, u kategoriji hidrotehničkih građevina.
2022
Pohvalnica Hrvatskih voda
Za doprinos projektiranju zaštite od štetnog djelovanja voda u porječju Drave.
2020
Godišnja nagrada Grada Osijeka
Za dugogodišnji doprinos komunalnoj infrastrukturi grada.
2018
IKA — priznanje za studiju utjecaja
Za studiju utjecaja na okoliš akumulacije Jankovac, primjer metodološke izvrsnosti.
03 / Kvaliteta

Održavanje kvalitete nije projekt — to je navika.

Naš sustav upravljanja kvalitetom oslanja se na ISO 9001 i na nekoliko jednostavnih internih pravila koja primjenjujemo doslovno na svakom zadatku.

ISO 9001 : 2015

Sustav upravljanja kvalitetom

Certificiran od 2016. godine, godišnji nadzorni auditi i kompletan trogodišnji recertifikacijski audit.

  • Registar projekata s jasno definiranom odgovornošću po fazi.
  • Kontrola dokumenata po načelu četveroočnog pregleda.
  • Zapisi o odstupanjima i korektivnim mjerama.
Interni standardi

Pravila koja svi znamo napamet

Kvaliteta se ne drži dokumentom — drži se navikom. Evo što provodimo bez iznimke.

  • Svaki projekt ima odgovornog inženjera od prvog dana do primopredaje.
  • Nijedan dokument ne izlazi iz ureda bez interne revizije.
  • Svaka izmjena zahtjeva ulazi u pisani trag.
  • Nadzor izvođenja obavlja inženjer koji je projekt i potpisao, gdje god je to moguće.
“Dobar projekt ne zaustavlja vodu. Pripitomi je — i iza nje ostavi krajolik koji i dalje diše.”
Ivan Horvat, direktor · 2024.

Dopuštamo si ovo kao program — ne samo kao rečenicu. Svaki projekt mjerimo ovim sitom prije nego što ga pošaljemo iz ureda.

, then update the root page handler and i18n config with the new routes, plus add translations for all the Hidroing sections.

Actually, I'm realizing there's a routing conflict here—the route group doesn't change the URL structure, so both `app/[lang]/page.tsx` and `app/[lang]/(hidroing)/page.tsx` would try to handle the same `/` path. The fix is to move the Hidroing home content directly into `app/[lang]/page.tsx` instead of nesting it in the route group. all other Hidroing pages in a `(hidroing)` route group for the shared layout.

Actually, for the home page specifically, I need to decide:
1. Replace `app/[lang]/page.tsx` entirely with the Hidroing home  
2. Or keep the `(index)` group pattern

I'll replace `app/[lang]/page.tsx` with the Hidroing home, and use `app/[lang]/(hidroing)/` for the layout-wrapping of inner pages.

But wait - the home page also needs the Nav and Footer. So I could:
- Put the home page in `(hidroing)` group too
- But that creates a conflict since `app/[lang]/page.tsx` already exists

The cleanest solution: Delete `app/[lang]/page.tsx` and move the home into `app/[lang]/(hidroing)/page.tsx`, then create the route group layout with Nav and Footer. This way everything—including the home page—gets wrapped with the shared navigation and footer components. the URL so it still handles `/`.

Let me structure it this way:
```
app/[lang]/
  (hydroing)/          ← route group (doesn't affect URL)
```

Pročišćavanje otpadnih voda P-042 / 2021 — 2023

UPOV Osijek — rekonstrukcija II. faze.

Rekonstrukcija i dogradnja gradskog uređaja za pročišćavanje otpadnih voda. Povećanje projektnog kapaciteta s 140.000 na 180.000 ekvivalent-stanovnika, uvođenje tercijarnog stupnja s uklanjanjem dušika i fosfora.

Lokacija
Osijek, HR
Naručitelj
Vodovod Osijek d.o.o.
Kapacitet
180.000 ES
Razdoblje
2021 — 2023

Tiha rekonstrukcija u punom pogonu.

Postrojenje je sve vrijeme rekonstrukcije bilo u pogonu. To je značilo fazno uvođenje novih građevina i procesnih jedinica uz strogu kontrolu bypass-a, bez prekida pročišćavanja i bez ispuštanja neobrađene vode u recipijent.

Tehnološko rješenje zadržava provjerenu liniju aktivacije i nadograđuje je selektorima za biološko uklanjanje dušika i fosfora. Linija mulja dobiva zgušnjivač i centrifugu, čime se smanjuje volumen zbrinjavanja za oko 35%.

Novi SCADA sustav povezuje crpne stanice u slivnom području s centralnim nadzorom uređaja, što otvara prostor za predikciju udarnih opterećenja po vremenskim uvjetima.

No old CSS class names remain in the home page. TypeScript is clean, the logo image exists at `/public/images/hidroing.png`, and `hidroing.css` is now 124 lines (down from ~700) containing only what Tailwind genuinely can't express.

Here's what changed:

**`styles/tailwind.css`** — Added 14 Hidroing tokens to `@theme`: `--color-ink` through `--color-blue-ink`, plus `--font-sans` and `--font-mono` pointing to the next/font variables. Updated `@layer base` to set `bg-paper text-ink font-sans` on `html/body`.

**`styles/hidroing.css`** — Stripped from ~700 lines to 124 lines. Only keeps: `:root` CSS vars, `.ph` placeholder gradients, `.reveal` scroll animation, `@keyframes marquee` + `.marquee-track`, and `form.enquiry` focus/select styles.

**All 10 files converted** to Tailwind utilities with `cn()` for conditional classes. Key patterns:
- Layout: `max-w-[1440px] mx-auto px-[clamp(20px,4vw,64px)]`
- Responsive type: `text-[clamp(40px,5.4vw,88px)]`
- Active nav underline: `after:absolute after:left-0 after:right-0 after:bottom-[-2px] after:h-px after:bg-green`
- Fractional grids: `grid-cols-[1.5fr_1fr_1fr_1fr]`
- Nav backdrop: `bg-paper/85 backdrop-blur-[8px] backdrop-saturate-[140%]`
